messages:
amina: heads-up — ran a focused perf/profile pass on Mistral-7B with FP8 KV cache + prefix prefetch. Seeing an odd combination of slab allocator fragmentation + kernel-router falling back to generic GEMM in tail cases. Posting top-line notes and logs.
amina: short summary: avg p95 token latency +18% on interactive traces with long prefixes (8k-12k), memory spikes due to small-slab churn, and ~30% of forward steps used generic kernel path for 1xN GEMMs instead of optimized attention kernel.
amina: raw profiler snapshot (filtered):
```
[profiler] sample: 2026-03-18T15:04:12Z
KV-cache slab: allocs=124k frees=123k active_slabs=47 fragmentation=0.23
Kernel-router: dispatched 71% fast-attn, 29% generic-gemm
Latency histogram (tokens): p50=12ms p95=48ms p99=98ms
Eviction events: 3.2k (LRU), TTL evict none
Memory RSS: 21.7G -> spike to 26.1G during heavy prefix warmup
```
amina: notes on model config: Mistral-7B default RoPE scaling (1.0), heads=32, kv-dim per-head 64. I tested alternate config: RoPE scale 0.5 + kv-dim 64 and also kv-dim 32.
riley: interesting — when kernel-router chooses generic-gemm is it because the sequence length or head dim falls to an unsupported shape? any router logs for the decision? 
amina: yes, router decision line: `router: shape=(32,1,4096)->policy=generic-gemm(reason=unoptimizedK)` where 1 is batch*seq for the inner loop. It triggers on fragmented batches (lots of single-seq rows) after per-request batching heuristics split odd shapes.
devon: does the batching heuristic produce many single-request steps? we've seen tail latency uplift when continuous batching doesn't coalesce prefixes. what are your batch-shaping params? 
amina: current heuristic: max_batch_tokens=4096, min_coalesce_time=5ms, prefer_prefetch=true. We observed many tiny batches when prefix cache hit rate drops (eviction churn). Prefetch warms KV cache but the slab allocator is not reusing freed small blocks efficiently.
jess: could be allocator fragmentation + cache pinning. If LRU evictions prune middle-of-prefix keys, subsequent prefetches allocate new slabs causing fragmentation. Have you tried a simple TTL-based eviction (coalesce evict windows) to reduce churn? 
amina: I ran TTL=60s vs LRU baseline. TTL reduced fragmentation to ~0.08 but increased steady-state memory by ~6% (fewer evicts). p95 latency improved ~6% vs LRU for long-prefix traces but cold-start p50 got worse for short-context (understandable).
riley: what about quantized-KV layout — are you storing FP8 as packed bytes or aligning to 16B lanes? alignment could amplify slab waste for small keys.
amina: stored as packed FP8 with 16-byte alignment padding per row for SSE/AVX path. The alignment means small-head dims (kv-dim=32) waste more. Changing layout to tightly-packed reduced RSS by ~0.9G but broke vectorized kernels on older GPUs, so fallback to scalar path kills perf.
devon: so multiple tradeoffs: tight packing saves memory but triggers slow fallback kernels; relaxed alignment keeps fast kernels but wastes memory and aggravates slab fragmentation. Kernel-router also seems to prefer fast-attn only when head_dim % 64 == 0; with kv-dim=32 we lost that path.
jess: have you tried making the router treat packed-FP8-as-fast if it sees a packed flag (i.e., teach kernels to accept packed layout)? possibly a one-off kernel that unpacks 64B lanes. Complexity vs benefit? 
amina: prototype kernel that decodes packed FP8 on the fly exists but adds ~6% per-token compute overhead for decode+permute. Net effect: memory down 1.0G, p95 down ~3% from baseline (because we avoid generic-gemm), but p50 up 4% due to decode cost. Mixed results.
perf-bot: alert: recent canary (runtime v2.14.1) shows 12% increase in p99 token tail for Mistral-7B across internal benchmark fleet. Linked traces: https://perf.internal/runs/1855006
riley: good catch. Could be rollout of new allocator optimizations in v2.14.1. Which commit? devon? 
devon: that was my change (slab freelist per-thread to reduce global lock contention). It reduced contention but I didn't stress long prefix workloads with FP8 kv. Sounds like freelist sizing interacted poorly with small-slab reuse. My bad.
amina: no worries — this is a useful find. Proposed experiment matrix (short):
- A: revert per-thread freelist -> baseline (quick repro)
- B: keep freelist + increase per-thread freebucket sizes for small slabs (16->64)
- C: TTL eviction with larger prefetch window (prefetch N=8 vs 4)
- D: kv-layout change (packed-tight) + packed-aware kernel or decode-kernel
- E: batching heuristic tweak: min_coalesce_time 10ms + prefer_batch_by_seqlen=true
Each run: 1000 interactive traces (varied prefix lengths), record p50/p95/p99, RSS median, allocator fragmentation, kernel-router stats.
amina: suggested run order: A (fast revert) -> B -> E -> C -> D. A/B/E are low-risk quick wins. D requires kernel work and perf testing on older GPUs.
jess: +1. also add a metric: fraction of steps hitting generic-gemm. that's our immediate correlate to p95.
arina: (typo) meant amina: I'll schedule these on canary pool this afternoon and post results.
riley: when you run A/B include a debug flag to log router reasons: `--router-debug=on` and `--kv-slab-stats=verbose`.
devon: I'll prepare a small patch that increases freelist bucket sizes and a fallback that trims free lists on memory pressure.
perf-bot: task created: PERF-1849 investigate Mistral FP8 kv fragmentation (assignee=amina, devon) due 2026-03-20
amina: action items: 1) revert and repro (A) 2) land freelist sizing patch (B) 3) run batching tweak E on canary 4) if still issues, schedule kernel work for packed-KV decode (D). I'll push repro script and traces to the shared gist when done.
riley: thanks — very clear. ping me after A completes and I'll coordinate console alerts so customers on dedicated can't hit p99 regressions.
amina: thanks all. uploading repro snippet now:
```bash
# run repro harness
python infra/tests/repro_kv_prefetch.py --model mistral-7b --kv-format fp8 --prefix-lens 2k,6k,10k --runs 1000 --router-debug on
```
amina: attaching sample trace (trimmed):
```
[trace] id=abc123 step=142
router=generic-gemm reason=unoptimizedK
kv: slab_alloc id=47 size=2048 head_slot=9
```
jess: solid. keep the messages coming, and if you need help with kernel prototyping tell me and I can pair with you on the decode microkernel.
amina: will do. ending thread with planned run times: A at 16:30 UTC, B at 18:00 UTC, E overnight. I'll post numbers as separate threads for each run.
